note: Rules-enforced Pro deck (server hero kenshiro), mirrored from unmatched.cards deck 6rDz "Kenshiro" by Calton_White, version WvW4T24Nq — the SAME source the engine converted from (data/heroes/kenshiro.rules.ts cites it), so every rules-relevant field here is engine-exact. A LAB deck: engine JollyGrin/unbrewed-engine#362 on the #359/#360 train, and four printed clauses are still BLOCKED engine-side (the Hundred-Fist chain, the 708-Meridian tick, and the two damage-taken reads on YOU ARE ALREADY DEAD! / Dragon Form), so balance and mechanics are not final. ART comes from the author's OTHER publication of this deck, the-unmatched.club 12653 (https://www.the-unmatched.club/c/heroes/kenshiro.12653), where he uploaded finished renders as per-card `replacementImage`; 6rDz itself only hotlinks scattered stock images. Every face, his `cardsBack`, and his `customImage` hero render are mirrored into public/evergreen-decks/art/6rDz (upstream they are i.imgur.com hotlinks and imgur rots; #446 standard) and drawn full-bleed via cardImage — never through the generated card template, which cannot reproduce his banners and layout, and never through the art-generation pipeline. URLs are repo-relative (Luke/Malfurion precedent) so the art resolves on localhost and preview builds too. token-kenshiro.webp is a bust cropped from that cardback art. KNOWN ART/RULES DIVERGENCE — the two upstream publications are not identical, and where they disagree this snapshot follows 6rDz (= the engine), so three cards print a boost pip that is one lower than the boost the referee applies: Momentous Shift (art 2, rules 3), Skirmish (art 1, rules 2) and Disrupting Strike (art 1, rules 2). The club copy also truncates Death Omen Star's text mid-sentence and banners Stone Mountain Splitting Slash as "Any" where its own art reads KENSHIRO; 6rDz is right on both. Upstream authoring conflict, flagged for the deck author — do NOT "fix" it here in either direction without a ruling. Titles/values/boosts/quantities are verbatim, typos included ("damege", "Drawn 2 cards", "form the game") — art matches by lowercased verbatim title. The three HOKUTO stages printed on Hundred-Fist Rush (WAAAA / TATATA / WAATAAA!) are the sub-attack chain engine#359's followup queue drains — see lib/pro/subAttackChain.ts for the client-side narration.
